title: PAP: the password does not match the stored password
plain_english: Everything up to the password check worked: the user was found and the backend returned a password (cleartext or a hash). The password the client sent does not match it. The line just above this one in the debug output ('Comparing with "known good" ...') names the attribute the server compared against, which is the important clue when the password is actually right.

causes.cause: Plain wrong password on the client, including a stale saved one.
causes.next_check: Run radtest on the server with the exact credentials; watch for trailing whitespace, keyboard layout, and a password recently changed in the directory.

causes.cause: Hash type confusion: the backend returns a hash but it is mapped to Cleartext-Password, or the hash has no {SSHA}/{crypt} header so the server compares the wrong way.
causes.next_check: Read the 'Comparing with "known good"' line: if it says Cleartext-Password but your directory stores hashes, fix the attribute mapping (ldap 'update' section, or sql's password column and Password-With-Header).

causes.cause: Two backends returned a password and the wrong one won: a users-file entry or a stale SQL row overrides the directory.
causes.next_check: In the authorize section of the debug output, find every module that added a password attribute for this request; the first one is the one pap compares.
